author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Map a PlayStation-style Bluetooth controller for PS2
summary: Pair through Android, verify the active controller mode, bind familiar PlayStation positions without assuming pressure support, test sticks and triggers, and confirm the Bluetooth profile survives sleep and reconnect.
heroAlt: PCSX2 DualShock 2 mapping screen with face buttons, sticks, shoulders, and force feedback

sourceLabels.android-game-controller: Android controller events, axes, and device behavior

blocks.text: Verify Android recognition before preserving familiar labels

A PlayStation-style shell makes the face-button positions familiar, but Android may expose the device through a compatibility mode with different axis codes or missing features. Pair it in Android settings, confirm it appears as a game controller, and map one Port 1 profile. Bind Cross, Circle, Square, and Triangle by their physical locations, then verify sticks, triggers, touchpad-derived buttons, and the PS button without assigning system-reserved actions accidentally.

Do not assume a modern controller reproduces DualShock 2 pressure-sensitive face buttons. Treat ordinary button presses as digital unless the exact device and emulator path expose verified analog values.

items: Controller charged and paired directly through Android Bluetooth settings.
Old duplicate pairings removed only after their identity is recorded.
One known controller mode selected and documented.
Existing Port 1 profile backed up.
A title that tests sticks, shoulders, menus, and vibration where supported.
1. Wake the controller and confirm Android reports it as connected before opening the emulator.
2. Create a named profile containing model and Bluetooth mode.
3. Bind face buttons, D-pad, shoulders, triggers, clicks, Start, and Select systematically.
4. Move each analog control slowly and verify neutral plus full range.
5. Test the mapping in a menu and a playable scene.
6. Put the controller to sleep, wake it, and confirm the same device profile returns.
7. Restart Android Bluetooth and repeat one reconnect cycle.
8. Record unsupported features rather than filling them with unrelated system buttons.

blocks.text: Naming the profile by model and mode prevents two logical variants from being merged. Sleep and Bluetooth restart tests reveal whether Android assigns a new device instance or whether the emulator restores the expected mapping reliably.
The controller passes when its complete functional layout survives ordinary wireless lifecycle changes.

items: Android recognizes the device before app launch.
Face-button positions match PS2 prompts.
Sticks center and reach full travel.
Sleep and wake preserve Port 1 assignment.
Unsupported pressure or touchpad behavior is documented clearly.
A generic keyboard profile appears: change only to a documented gamepad mode and re-pair.
Axes change after reconnect: remove the stale logical-device profile and rebuild once.
The PS button opens system UI: leave it unbound inside the game profile.
Low battery causes disconnects: charge before evaluating mapping stability.

blocks.text: Return to the prior pairing and input profile
Forget only the failed pairing, reconnect in the recorded original mode, import the known-good Port 1 mapping, and cold-boot the test title. Preserve other Bluetooth audio and controller devices.
Controller branding does not guarantee Android feature parity

Official and third-party PlayStation-style devices can expose different vibration, touchpad, motion, pressure, and battery features. Accept only behaviors observed on the tested Android path. Treat the PS button and touchpad click carefully because Android or the controller firmware may reserve them for system actions. A profile passes only when ordinary gameplay controls, sleep and wake, battery recovery, and a cold Bluetooth reconnect all restore the same Port 1 identity without adding a duplicate interface.
